programs.name: Heavy Lifter: 4-Day Strength & Hypertrophy
programs.description: Advanced heavy powerbuilding program simulating an experienced heavy lifter. High compound loads on bench, squat, deadlift and rows with targeted hypertrophy accessories.
guidelines: Train Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday. Rest 3 to 5 minutes on heavy compound working sets.
Warm up thoroughly using 2–3 lighter ramp sets before logging working sets.
Prioritize explosive concentric speed and strict control on the negative.
When target reps are achieved with solid form, increase load by 2.5 kg next microcycle.

programs.name: Aesthetic Engine: 5-Day Hypertrophy
programs.description: For experienced lifters who enjoy five gym days. Balanced upper/lower muscle building with extra shoulder work. Full gym; roughly 55–75 minutes per session.
guidelines: Train Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday. Keep Wednesday and Sunday free for recovery; add time between sessions if recovery suffers.
The listed sets are working sets. Warm up first, then use progressively heavier practice sets before your first heavy lifts.
Finish most sets with about 2 good repetitions left. Keep the same controlled range of motion; failure is not required.
When every set reaches the top of its rep range with clean form, increase by the smallest available weight next time and return to the lower end. Otherwise keep the weight and build reps.
Keep the plan for 6–8 weeks before judging progress. If fatigue accumulates or performance drops across several sessions, use fewer sets and lighter loads for a week. Do not train through pain.

programs.name: Athletic Engine: 3-Day Strength & Power
programs.description: General strength and low-rep power practice for experienced lifters, not a sport-specific conditioning plan. Full gym with trap bar, kettlebell and low platform; about 50–65 minutes.
guidelines: Train on non-consecutive days and account for your sport sessions. Learn swings and push presses before using this plan. Use light-to-moderate loads on these two lifts and stop the set as soon as speed or technique drops, even before the target reps.
Do not apply automatic rep-range progression to swings or push presses: add load only while every repetition stays fast and controlled. This plan does not replace aerobic training or sport practice.
The listed sets are working sets. Warm up first, then use progressively heavier practice sets before your first heavy lifts.
Finish most sets with about 2 good repetitions left. Keep the same controlled range of motion; failure is not required.
When every set reaches the top of its rep range with clean form, increase by the smallest available weight next time and return to the lower end. Otherwise keep the weight and build reps.
Keep the plan for 6–8 weeks before judging progress. If fatigue accumulates or performance drops across several sessions, use fewer sets and lighter loads for a week. Do not train through pain.
